summary.headline: IG Petrochemicals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 63% to Rs 770 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18% vs 5.8% a year earlier, on higher realisations.
summary.overview: Management reported the highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 770 crore (up 63% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 144 crore versus Rs 27 crore a year earlier, driven mainly by better realisations while volumes were slightly lower. H1 FY27 revenue rose 46% to Rs 1,390 crore and EBITDA rose to Rs 266 crore. The green-feed plasticizer plant started production on 30 September 2026 with 75,000 tpa initial capacity, and the CBG plant is expected to start by end-December. The board declared an interim dividend of Rs 10 per share (100% of face value).

financial_highlights.value: Rs 10 per share (100% of Rs 10 face value)

segments.name: Phthalic anhydride (PA) - core
segments.commentary: Three plants operating in Q2 at 90-91% utilisation of operating capacity; fourth plant recently started. Volume rose 15-18% QoQ to above 47 (units as stated, quantity not disclosed); FY27 guidance about 2 lakh tonnes (+/-3-4%).

segments.name: Plasticizers (DOP, DINP etc.)
segments.commentary: Production started 30 September 2026 with 75,000 tpa initial capacity; early supply 1,000-1,500 tonnes pending quality approvals. Management expects 10,000-15,000 tonnes ramp in the near term and 40,000-50,000 tonnes next year, focus on DOP and DINP for wire and cable.

segments.name: Maleic anhydride (MA) and by-products
segments.commentary: MA from wash water: about Rs 20-21 crore in Q2 vs Rs 14-15 crore average in earlier quarters; by-product revenue of Rs 39-40 crore in Q2 with benzoic acid at Rs 1-2 crore. MA priced about 10-15% below phthalic anhydride (MA Rs 150-160 vs PA Rs 180-190 per unit as stated).

segments.name: Benzoic acid (BP)
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded from about 8,000 to 12,000 tpa; expected to contribute meaningfully over the next four to five years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PA volume guidance about 2 lakh tonnes (+/-3-4%), management says on track.
Plasticizer volumes for FY27 expected at 185,000-195,000 tonnes total; FY28 net saleable volume about 2.10-2.15 lakh tonnes after captive consumption of 20,000-25,000 tonnes of PA.

Plasticizer plant could reach 60,000-75,000 tpa in FY28-29 depending on customer penetration; management expects peak revenue of Rs 3,000-3,500 crore at normalised prices (plasticizer net revenue about Rs 500 crore).
Management expects spreads to stay healthy but would not commit to sustainability; cites a cutoff of about USD 200-250/t for new plants.
CBG plant to start operations by end-December 2026.
Interim dividend of Rs 10 per share declared.
capex_capacity: Green-feed plasticizer plant started 30 September 2026; initial capacity 75,000 tpa, expandable to about 1,00,000 tpa.
Fourth PA plant started; three to four plants run at a time with one under maintenance.
Benzoic acid capacity raised from about 8,000 to 12,000 tpa.
CBG plant fully set up; commissioning expected by end-December 2026.

Solar power in use at the Dahej plant (netted off existing bills for four years); evaluating solar for the plasticizer plant. Shift from LSFO to natural gas underway (about 80% of fuel is natural gas; gas about 10% cheaper than LSFO per management).
Management said any new downstream project must clear a minimum 15% IRR; none approved by the board yet.
Abu Dhabi JV investment property (over Rs 200 crore) being sold; sale expected in 6-9 months.
demand_pricing: Spreads volatile: Rs 300-400 per unit (as stated, likely USD/t) in the market recently, about 100-200 in the prior six months; company earns about USD 100 over market spreads.
Industry plants at 60-70% utilisation due to feedstock shortages linked to Middle East disruption (Hormuz, Red Sea); feedstock prices up 30-60% in six months per management.

Domestic demand strong across paints, pigments, plasticizers and UPR; growth in specialty chemicals, agrochemicals, UPR and PVC. Plasticizer demand growing 5-6% (cable segment cited at 50-60% as stated).
Inventory kept minimal; 80-85% of sales booked against procurement to limit price volatility.
Inventory gain in Q2 less than 2% of profit per management.
Competitor (unnamed) volumes about 10,000-11,000 tpa, with management attributing its weaker performance to a US facility, interest burden and depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: What are utilisation, volume and spread data for the quarter and currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose absolute volumes; volume rose 15-18% QoQ. Operating plants ran at 90-91% utilisation. Spreads 300-400 currently, 100-200 over the prior six months; sustainability not committed due to feedstock constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Will the spread sustain and what is the cycle view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on spread levels, saying they are a function of demand-supply and geopolitics. Cited USD 200-250/t as the cutoff for new-plant economics, and conversion cost of about USD 150/t in South Asia.

qa_highlights.question: Will PA5 and plasticizer ramp add to domestic supply and pressure prices?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PA guidance about 2 lakh tonnes; FY28 incremental capacity about 15,000 tonnes net saleable after captive use of 30,000-40,000 tonnes of PA for DOP and plasticizer.

qa_highlights.question: How is the plasticizer ramp and qualification proceeding?
qa_highlights.answer: Two to three batches produced; quality checks underway with supply starting around mid-to-end of quarter; ramp 10,000-15,000 tpa initially, 40,000-50,000 tpa next year, with 60,000-75,000 tpa possible later.

qa_highlights.question: Margins and profitability of by-products (MA, benzoic acid)?
qa_highlights.answer: MA about Rs 20-21 crore in Q2 vs Rs 14-15 crore average earlier; by-product revenue about Rs 39-40 crore; benzoic acid Rs 1-2 crore. MA priced about 10-15% below PA.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition plans and use of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is looking at downstream acquisitions but a competitor acquisition unlikely due to CCI concerns (combined 80% Indian capacity). Dividend of Rs 10 per share is small relative to cash.

risks_watch: Spread sustainability once Middle East supply disruption eases; management expects moderation in both feedstock and product prices after war ends.
Plasticizer ramp dependent on customer qualification and quality approvals; FY28 volumes not yet committed.
Feedstock (ortho-xylene and related) cost elevated; logistics costs up 2-3x per management.
Inventory gain and by-product contribution may fluctuate; other income contribution sizeable.
Abu Dhabi property sale expected in 6-9 months; ~Rs 200 crore of cash to be realised.
Unnamed downstream and acquisition plans not yet board approved.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and demand, but cautious and evasive on forward spreads, timing of plasticizer volumes and new projects, repeatedly declining to commit beyond current conditions. Transcript quality was poor, with many garbled passages.
key_quotes: IGPL has delivered a very strong quarterly performance, achieving the highest ever quarterly revenue along with the Saab improvement in the profitability compared to the corresponding quarter for previous year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 18% vs 5.8% a year ago on spreads of Rs 300-400/unit now vs 100-200 earlier, but management would not commit to spread sustainability and expects moderation once Middle East disruption eases.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plasticizer plant (75,000 tpa) started 30 Sep 2026 with 1,000-1,500 t early supply, CBG plant to start by end-Dec 2026, and fourth PA plant already running at 90-91% utilisation of operating capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 PA guidance about 2 lakh t (+/-3-4%) held and plasticizer FY27 volume guided at 185,000-195,000 t, though Q2 volumes were slightly lower and plasticizer ramp is only 10,000-15,000 t initially and not yet customer-committed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Operating plants at 90-91% utilisation and a plasticizer expansion to 1,00,000 tpa is possible, but no new downstream project has been approved by the board and any project must clear a 15% IRR hurdle.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue up 46% to Rs 1,390 crore and FY27 volume guidance was only held, not raised; upside depends on spreads holding while feedstock constraints persist.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects spreads and feedstock prices to moderate after the Middle East war ends, and plasticizer FY28 volumes are not yet committed to customers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Plasticizer (DOP, DINP for wire and cable) supply began around quarter-end with 1,000-1,500 t shipped pending quality approvals, and CBG plant is due by end-December 2026.

rows.label: Plasticizer ramp to 40-50k t next year
rows.why: Management plans 10-15k t near-term ramp and 40-50k t next year on the 75k tpa plant, with peak plasticizer revenue of Rs 3,000-3,500 crore at normalised prices, though customer qualification is pending.

rows.label: Abu Dhabi property sale
rows.why: Investment property over Rs 200 crore being sold, adding to net cash of Rs 150 crore as of September.

rows.label: Spread normalisation risk
rows.why: Spreads rose to Rs 300-400/unit from Rs 100-200 over six months; industry plants at 60-70% utilisation on feedstock shortages, and management expects moderation after war ends.

tone.note: Management was confident on the quarter's results, demand and plasticizer launch, but cautious and evasive on forward spreads, plasticizer volume timing and new projects; analysts pressed on spread sustainability and capacity additions, and the transcript was poor quality.
